questions.question:
Consider a processor [latex]\text{P}[/latex] whose instruction set architecture is the load-store architecture. The instruction format is such that the first operand of any instruction is the destination operand.

Which one of the following sequences of instructions corresponds to the high-level language statement [latex]{Z}={X}+{Y}[/latex] ?
Note: X, Y, and Z are memory operands. R[latex]0[/latex], R[latex]1[/latex], and R[latex]2[/latex] are registers.

options.B:
LOAD R[latex]0[/latex], X
ADD Z, R[latex]0[/latex], Y
options.C:
ADD R[latex]0[/latex], X, Y
STORE Z, R[latex]0[/latex]
options.D:
LOAD R[latex]0[/latex], X
LOAD R[latex]1[/latex], Y
ADD R[latex]2[/latex], R[latex]0[/latex], R[latex]1[/latex]
STORE Z, R[latex]2[/latex]

questions.explanation:
In a load-store (register-register) architecture, arithmetic instructions can only operate on registers, never directly on memory. So to compute [latex]Z=X+Y[/latex] where [latex]X,Y,Z[/latex] are memory locations, we must:

1. LOAD both memory operands into registers: [latex]\text{LOAD } R0, X[/latex] and [latex]\text{LOAD } R1, Y[/latex].
2. Perform the addition on registers: [latex]\text{ADD } R2, R0, R1[/latex] (destination is first operand, per the given convention).
3. STORE the result back to memory: [latex]\text{STORE } Z, R2[/latex].

Any option that uses a memory operand directly inside an ADD instruction (e.g. [latex]\text{ADD } Z, X, Y[/latex] or [latex]\text{ADD } Z, R0, Y[/latex]) is invalid for a load-store machine, since ADD can only take register operands.

Answer: LOAD R0,X; LOAD R1,Y; ADD R2,R0,R1; STORE Z,R2

questions.question: A cache memory that has a hit rate of 0.8 has an access latency 10 ns and miss penalty 100 ns. An optimization is done on the cache to reduce the miss rate. However, the optimization results in an increase of cache access latency to 15 ns, whereas the miss penalty is not affected. The minimum hit rate (rounded off to two decimal places) needed after the optimization such that it should not increase the average memory access time is _____.
questions.explanation:
Average memory access time = hit latency + miss rate [latex]\times[/latex] miss penalty.

Before: [latex]10+0.2\times100=30[/latex] ns.
After: [latex]15+(1-h)\times100\le30\Rightarrow1-h\le0.15\Rightarrow h\ge0.85[/latex]

Answer: 0.85

questions.question:
Match each addressing mode in [latex]\textbf{List I}[/latex] with a data element or an element of a data structure (in a high-level language) in [latex]\textbf{List II}[/latex]:

[latex] \begin{array}{|l|l|} \hline {\textbf{List I}} & {\textbf{List II}} \\ \hline \hline P.\ \text{Immediate} & 1.\ \text{Element of an array} \\ \hline Q.\ \text{Indirect} & 2.\ \text{Pointer} \\ \hline R.\ \text{Base with index} & 3.\ \text{Element of a record} \\ \hline S.\ \text{Base with offset/displacement} & 4.\ \text{Constant} \\ \hline \end{array} [/latex]
questions.explanation:
Matching addressing modes to the high-level data element they naturally implement:

- P. Immediate: the operand value is embedded directly in the instruction → used for a Constant (4).
- Q. Indirect: the instruction holds the address of the address of data → used to implement a Pointer (2).
- R. Base with index: effective address = base + index, naturally used to access an Element of an array (1) (base = array start, index = subscript).
- S. Base with offset/displacement: effective address = base + fixed offset, naturally used to access an Element of a record/struct (3) (base = record start, offset = field position).

Answer: P-4, Q-2, R-1, S-3

questions.question:
Consider a disk with the following specifications: rotation speed of 6000 RPM,
average seek time of 5 milliseconds, 500 sectors/track, 512-byte sectors.
A file has content stored in 3000 sectors located randomly on the disk. Assuming
average rotational latency, the total time (in seconds, rounded off to 2 decimal
places) to read the entire file from the disk is _______
questions.explanation:
6000 RPM = 100 rotations/s [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] one rotation = 10 ms, average rotational latency = 5 ms.
Transfer time of one sector [latex]=10/500=0.02[/latex] ms.

Sectors are random, so each needs seek + latency + transfer:
[latex]5+5+0.02=10.02[/latex] ms

Total [latex]=3000\times10.02\text{ ms}=30.06[/latex] s

Answer: 30.06

questions.question:
The size of the physical address space of a processor is [latex]2^{32}[/latex] bytes. The capacity of a cache memory unit is [latex]2^{23}[/latex] bytes. The cache block size is [latex]128[/latex] bytes. The cache memory unit can be built as a direct mapped cache or as a [latex]K[/latex]-way set-associative cache, where [latex]K=2^{L}[/latex] and [latex]L \in\{1,2,3\}[/latex]. Let the length of the TAG field be [latex]M[/latex] bits for the direct mapped cache, and [latex]N[/latex] bits for the set-associative cache.

Which one of the following options is true?
questions.explanation:
Given: address space [latex]=2^{32}[/latex] bytes, cache size [latex]=2^{23}[/latex] bytes, block size [latex]=128=2^7[/latex] bytes.

Direct-mapped cache: number of cache lines [latex]=\dfrac{2^{23}}{2^7}=2^{16}[/latex], so index field [latex]=16[/latex] bits, offset field [latex]=7[/latex] bits. Tag field [latex]M=32-16-7=9[/latex] bits.

[latex]K[/latex]-way set-associative cache ([latex]K=2^L[/latex]): number of sets [latex]=\dfrac{2^{16}}{2^L}=2^{16-L}[/latex], so index field [latex]=16-L[/latex] bits, offset field still [latex]=7[/latex] bits. Tag field [latex]N=32-(16-L)-7=9+L[/latex] bits.

Comparing: [latex]N=9+L=M+L[/latex] (since [latex]M=9[/latex]).

Answer: [latex]N=M+L[/latex]

questions.question:
Consider a system with [latex]1[/latex] MB physical memory and a word length of [latex]1[/latex] byte. The system uses a direct mapped cache, with block numbers starting from [latex]0[/latex]. The word with physical address [latex]\text{0xA2C28}[/latex] is mapped to the cache block number [latex]176_{10}[/latex]. The maximum possible size of the cache (in KB ) for this configuration is ________. (answer in integer)
Note: [latex]1 {~K}=2^{10}[/latex] and [latex]1 {M}=2^{20}[/latex]
questions.explanation:
Physical address [latex]0\text{xA2C28}[/latex] in [latex]20[/latex]-bit binary is [latex]10100010110000101000[/latex] (since [latex]1[/latex] MB [latex]=2^{20}[/latex] bytes). We're told this maps to cache block index [latex]176=10110000_2[/latex] ([latex]8[/latex] bits).

To maximize the cache size, we want to find offset width [latex]b[/latex] and index width [latex]L[/latex] (cache size [latex]=2^{b+L}[/latex] bytes) such that the [latex]L[/latex]-bit field of the address immediately above the [latex]b[/latex]-bit offset exactly equals [latex]176[/latex], while making [latex]b+L[/latex] as large as possible (equivalently, keeping the remaining tag field as short as possible, but non-zero, since it must still be consistent with the given index value's exact bit-pattern).

Checking all valid alignments of the address's bits, the largest working combination is offset [latex]b=6[/latex] bits (block size [latex]64[/latex] bytes) and index [latex]L=11[/latex] bits ([latex]2048[/latex] lines), which correctly extracts index [latex]=00010110000_2=176[/latex] and leaves a [latex]3[/latex]-bit tag ([latex]101_2[/latex]) — consistent with the [latex]20[/latex]-bit address ([latex]3+11+6=20[/latex]).

Maximum cache size [latex]=2^{b+L}=2^{17}=131072[/latex] bytes [latex]=128[/latex] KB.

Answer: 128

questions.question: The stage delays in a 4-stage pipeline are 800,500,400 and 300 picoseconds.The first stage (with delay 800 picoseconds)is replaced with a functionally equivalent design involving two stages with respective delays 600 and 350 picoseconds.The throughput increase of the pipeline is ________ percent.

questions.question: Consider a 3GHz (gigahertz) processor with a three-stage pipeline and stage latencies [latex]\tau _{1}[/latex], [latex]\tau _{2}[/latex], and [latex]\tau _{3}[/latex] such that [latex]\tau _{1}=3\tau _{2}/4=2\tau _{3}[/latex]. If the longest pipeline stage is split into two pipeline stages of equal latency, the new frequency is _____GHz, ignoring delays in the pipeline registers.

Let [latex]\tau_1=6k[/latex]: then [latex]\tau_2=8k[/latex] and [latex]\tau_3=3k[/latex]. The clock is set by the longest stage, 8k, at 3 GHz.

New frequency [latex]=3\times\frac{8k}{6k}=4[/latex] GHz

questions.question:
Consider a main memory system that consists of 8 memory modules attached to the system
bus, which is one word wide. When a write request is made, the bus is occupied for 100
nanoseconds (ns) by the data, address, and control signals. During the same 100 ns, and for
500 ns thereafter, the addressed memory module executes one cycle accepting and storing the data. The (internal) operation of different memory modules may overlap in time, but only one request can be on the bus at any time. The maximum number of stores (of one word each) that can be initiated in 1 millisecond is ____________
questions.subtopic: ALU Data Path and Control Unit
questions.explanation:
Each store holds the bus for 100 ns, and a module is busy for 600 ns. With 8 modules used in turn, a module is reused only after 8 [latex]\times[/latex] 100 = 800 ns [latex]\gt[/latex] 600 ns, so modules never cause waiting.

The bus is the bottleneck: one store per 100 ns.

[latex]\frac{1\,ms}{100\,ns}=\frac{10^{-3}}{10^{-7}}=10^4[/latex]

Answer: 10000

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.question: A processor [latex]X_1[/latex] operating at 2 GHz has a standard 5-stage RISC instruction pipeline having a base CPI (cycles per instruction) of one without any pipeline hazards. For a given program P that has 30% branch instructions, control hazards incur 2 cycles stall for every branch. A new version of the processor [latex]X_2[/latex] operating at same clock frequency has an additional branch predictor unit (BPU) that completely eliminates stalls for correctly predicted branches. There is neither any savings nor any additional stalls for wrong predictions. There are no structural hazards and data hazards for [latex]X_1[/latex] and [latex]X_2[/latex]. If the BPU has a prediction accuracy of 80%, the speed up (rounded   off to   two decimal places)   obtained   by [latex]X_2[/latex]    over   [latex]X_1[/latex]   in executing P is
questions.explanation:
Compare the CPI of both processors:
- [latex]X_1[/latex]: CPI [latex]=1+0.3\times2=1.6[/latex]
- [latex]X_2[/latex]: only the 20% wrongly predicted branches stall: CPI [latex]=1+0.3\times0.2\times2=1.12[/latex]

Same clock, so speedup [latex]=\frac{1.6}{1.12}\approx1.43[/latex]

Answer: 1.43

questions.question:
Consider an instruction pipeline with five stages without any branch prediction: Fetch Instruction
(FI), Decode Instruction (DI), Fetch Operand (FO), Execute Instruction (EI) and Write Operand
(WO). The stage delays for FI, DI, FO, EI and WO are 5 ns, 7 ns, 10 ns, 8 ns and 6 ns, respectively.
There are intermediate storage buffers after each stage and the delay of each buffer is 1 ns. A
program consisting of 12 instructions I1, I2, I3,..., I12 is executed in this pipelined processor.
Instruction I4 is the only branch instruction and its branch target is I9. If the branch is taken during
the execution of this program, the time (in ns) needed to complete the program is
questions.explanation:
Clock = slowest stage + buffer = 10 + 1 = 11 ns.

I4 is a branch, resolved after its EI stage (cycle 7). I5-I8 are discarded and I9 is fetched in cycle 8. I9-I12 then finish at cycle 8 + 4 + 3 = 15.

Time = 15 [latex]\times[/latex] 11 = 165 ns

Answer: 165

questions.question:
A processor has 16 integer registers (R0, R1,...,R15) and 64 floating point registers (F0, F1,...,F63). It uses a 2-byte instruction format. There are four categories of instructions: Type-1, Type-2, Type-3, and Type-4. Type-1 category consists of four instructions, each with 3 integer register operands (3Rs). Type-2 category consists of eight instructions, each with 2 floating point register operands (2Fs). Type-3 category consists of fourteen instructions, each with one integer register operand and one floating point register operand (1R+1F). Type-4 category consists of N instructions, each with a floating point register operand (1F).
The maximum value of N is __________.
questions.explanation:
Integer register = 4 bits, FP register = 6 bits, instruction = 16 bits. Use expanding opcodes:
- Type-1 (12 operand bits): 4-bit opcode, uses 4 of 16 codes.
- Type-2 (12 bits): 4-bit opcode, uses 8 codes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4 left.
- Type-3 (10 bits): 6-bit opcode: 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 = 16 codes, uses 14 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 left.
- Type-4 (6 bits): 10-bit opcode: 2 [latex]\times[/latex] [latex]2^4[/latex] = 32.

Answer: 32
